subject.title: Feature: channels.slack.ignoreSubtypes config key to suppress message_changed / message_deleted events

question: Should Slack edit/delete system events remain default session events, become suppressible through a new `channels.slack.ignoreSubtypes` config key, or be dropped by default?
rationale: The source-level problem is clear, but OpenClaw policy sets a high bar for new config keys and this choice changes public Slack event semantics.

options.title: Add opt-in ignoreSubtypes
options.body: Add a narrow Slack plugin config key for approved subtype suppression while preserving existing default behavior and special Assistant/thread-broadcast paths.

options.title: Change default policy
options.body: Drop edit/delete events by default, which reduces unwanted wakeups but may remove existing observability for users relying on those system events.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Leave edit/delete as system events and document prompt or operational guidance instead of adding config surface.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in ignoreSubtypes
recommendation.body: Add a narrow Slack plugin config key for approved subtype suppression while preserving existing default behavior and special Assistant/thread-broadcast paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Most of the relevant Slack subtype behavior and later policy-preserving fixes trace through steipete's commits.
